pairs.description: Chamomile contains naturally occurring coumarin constituents that can potentiate the anticoagulant effects of warfarin and cause bleeding.
pairs.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant action combined with mild CYP2C9 metabolic inhibition by chamomile flavonoids.

pairs.description: Chamomile can inhibit intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes, increasing blood concentrations and renal toxicity risk of cyclosporine.
pairs.mechanism: Apigenin-mediated inhibition of CYP3A4 enzymes and enteric P-glycoprotein efflux pumps.

pairs.description: Concurrent ingestion of chamomile with aspirin can increase gastric mucosal bleeding risk and antiplatelet activity.
pairs.mechanism: Additive inhibition of platelet aggregation and synergistic gastric mucosal prostaglandin suppression.

pairs.description: Chamomile possesses mild central nervous system depressant and anxiolytic actions that can enhance drowsiness when combined with SSRIs.
pairs.mechanism: Apigenin binding to central benzodiazepine receptors producing additive somnolence with psychotropic drugs.
